cases.rationale: An intact v0.3 bundle as actions/attest-build-provenance writes it, signed by the test instance: every check passes.
A v0.2 bundle with an x509CertificateChain and the slsa-framework buildType that GitHub attestations of 2024 carry.
A v0.1 bundle carries the inclusion promise and no inclusion proof; the client MUST validate the promise (sigstore_bundle.proto, VerificationMaterial.tlog_entries).
npm provenance as npm publish --provenance writes it: a v0.2 bundle, a Rekor intoto 0.0.2 entry, a sha512 subject.
The relying party passes npm's dist.integrity (SRI) as the digest.
The npm publish attestation: a v0.1 Statement signed by the registry key named by hint.
Unrecognized predicate fields are ignored (SP-02) and null reads as unset (SP-03).
Ambiguous JSON: a second mediaType member. A last-wins parser and a first-wins parser read two bundles; the strict parser refuses it.
protojson reads verification_material as verificationMaterial; two spellings of one field are refused by name.
An unknown bundle version is not read.
A DSSE envelope in a bundle MUST have exactly one signature.
From bundle version 0.2 on, every log entry carries an inclusion proof.
A v0.1 log entry needs its inclusion promise.
The single-certificate form exists from version 0.3 on.
One payload byte changed after signing.
Ambiguous JSON inside the signed payload: the signature covers it, the statement is refused.
The leaf is issued by a CA outside the trusted root that carries the trusted intermediate's name; the log entry and SCT are otherwise intact.
The envelope is signed by a key that is not the leaf's.
The entry names a log the trusted root does not list.
The signed entry timestamp names the trusted log but is signed by another key.
The checkpoint over the proof's root is not signed by the log.
One audit-path hash changed: the proof no longer leads from the body to the root.
The log signed a checkpoint, but over another root than the proof's.
The leaf carries no SCT: it was not logged in a trusted CT log.
The only SCT comes from a CT log the trusted root does not list.
The log entry commits to another certificate than the bundle's.
The log entry commits to another payload than the envelope's.
A v0.3 bundle with an inclusion proof but no signed entry timestamp and no RFC 3161 timestamp: integratedTime is unsigned and MUST NOT be trusted.
No transparency-log entry where the relying party requires one log (the default).
The log signed a time one hour after the signing, when the ten-minute leaf had expired.
integratedTime was changed after the log signed the entry timestamp.
Signed and logged consistently under the registry's retired key, whose expiry (2026-01-01) precedes the log's signed time (2026-01-15).
With no log required (GitHub's private instance), a bundle still needs a verified time; an unsigned integratedTime is none.
A Fulcio leaf has an empty subject; the identity is the SAN.
One line under the log's key verifies, a second under the same key does not: rejected.
A trusted root whose Rekor logId is not the SHA-256 of the log key is unusable trust material.
npm's GitLab provenance (Statement v0.1, SLSA v0.2) is refused as not implemented, never read.
Two subject alternative names are two identities; a Fulcio leaf names one.
A sound attestation from another workflow of the same repository than the one expected.
The relying party expects another OIDC issuer.

The signed predicate names another repository than the certificate Fulcio issued. The comparison follows the producers' code, not a specification, so it is a note and the verdict stands (owner decision 2026-10-26).
A sound statement of another predicate type.
The GitHub profile reads in-toto Statement v1 only.
The envelope's payloadType is not application/vnd.in-toto+json.
A statement without a subject names no artifact.
runDetails.builder.id is REQUIRED in SLSA Provenance v1.
A buildType the profile does not read.
Consumers SHOULD reject unrecognized external parameters (actions/buildtypes workflow/v1).
A sound attestation about another artifact than the one the relying party holds.
The relying party expects another package version.
A v0.1 Statement requires a name on every subject.
The key hint names no key of the registry document.
kindVersion names another kind than the logged body has.
A note holds no control character but the newline.
A pad bit set in the root: the same bytes to a lenient decoder, refused as non-canonical.
Two signature lines with one key name and one key ID.
The proof's leaf index equals the tree size.
A member the TransparencyLogEntry message does not define.
A v0.2 chain that also carries the intermediate and the root: they are ignored, the chain is built from the trusted root.
DSSE fields in the URL-safe alphabet and no keyid: both are allowed.
A ResourceDescriptor needs one of uri, digest, content.
buildDefinition.externalParameters is REQUIRED.
A Timestamp field is an RFC 3339 string in UTC.
The relying party pins the numeric repository ID, which survives a rename.
Two DigestSets match if any field the relying party accepts matches.
A leaf whose version field is not v1, v2 or v3 is malformed, not an exception.
A trusted-root key on a curve the module cannot load is unusable trust material.
More log entries than the count bound of 32: 33 empty entries, refused before any is read (owner decision of 2026-10-26: empty entries instead of copies, under 10 KB).
An issuer alone accepts every GitHub workflow; the policy must name a workflow or repository.
DSSE says to ignore an unrecognized envelope field; in a bundle the envelope is read closed like every other message (a deviation from DSSE, named in the documentation).
The same deviation for a member of the envelope's one signature.
The actions.github.io buildType says resolvedDependencies MUST contain the source commit; a rule of the specification, so a failing check and not a note.
The slsa-framework buildType says resolvedDependencies SHOULD contain the source commit; its absence is reported in the binding note and decides no verdict.
The actions.github.io buildType MUST NOT be used for an event other than create, release, push or workflow_dispatch; predicate and certificate agree on pull_request.
The predicate says push, the certificate Fulcio issued says the run was triggered by pull_request_target: the run's event is the certificate's, and the buildType must not describe it.
The slsa-framework buildType carries the same rule in the same words (github-actions-buildtypes workflow/v1).
The slsa-framework buildType defines the external parameters inputs, release and vars beside workflow; a run of workflow_dispatch with inputs and vars is well formed.
At most one of inputs or release can be set (slsa-framework buildType).
workflow_dispatch is one of the four events the buildType names.
The registry's signature over name@version:integrity verifies under the registry key the keys document lists, valid at the publish attestation's verified time.
The signature is the registry key's, but over another version than the document names.
The signature's keyid names no key of the registry keys document (pacote: EMISSINGSIGNATUREKEY).
Signed by a registry key that expired 2026-01-01, before the publish attestation's verified time 2026-01-15 (pacote: EEXPIREDSIGNATUREKEY).
No dist.signatures although the registry publishes signing keys.
A sound registry signature over another tarball's integrity than the publish attestation names.
A sound registry signature for another version than the publish attestation names.
